description: Using `not` in prefix position as a boolean negation operator fires E-TYPE-045 (§42.10). `if (not @ready)` treats `not` as a negation operator, but `not` is the absence VALUE, not an operator — use `!expr` for boolean negation or `expr is not` for absence. The lowering choke-point reports E-TYPE-045. Incidental W-PROGRAM-SPA-INFERRED is ignored by superset matching.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 1 (g-boot-body-top-lift-render-s478, option (b)) — migrated: a body-top `${ … }` renders nothing (§17.3 amended S478)
rationale: §42.10 `not` is the absence value, never a prefix negation operator; a prefix `not expr` in any expression position is a compile error (E-TYPE-045), steering to `!expr` (negation) or `expr is not` (absence check). (S478 open-Qs ruling item 1: migrated from a body-top `${ if (…) { <p/> } }`, which renders nothing there and is E-MARKUP-STATEMENT-NOT-RENDERED (§17.3 amended S478), to the `if=` attribute form. The bootstrap has no E-TYPE-045: it reports a parse error at the `@` of `not @ready` — g-boot-e-type-045-prefix-not-s478.)
